title: Subscriber Retention Intelligence
summary: A governed retention analysis system over 442,211,685 accepted membership, payment, listening, and churn-label rows, with cutoff-safe cohorts, a calibrated repeat-subscriber model, and an assumption-bound intervention planner.
outcome: A subscription lifecycle analyst can locate material renewal and engagement changes, compare cohorts and segments on governed definitions, and test a finite contact program without confusing historical risk with causal treatment response.

disclaimer: This public project uses a transformed consumer subscription dataset under the owner-approved source terms. It is not confidential enterprise data. Release-specific keys replace source identifiers, exact age and registration date are generalized, and private tokens, model artifacts, publication salt, and private subscriber views are excluded. Historical churn association does not establish treatment response.

presentation.question: Which retention movements need investigation, and where could finite outreach be plausible without overstating the evidence?
presentation.answer: The product separates descriptive movement, calibrated historical risk, and simulated economics. The challenger is supported only for 881,701 repeat subscribers, improves log loss by 5.57 percent, and concentrates churn 4.95 times above baseline in the top decile. Contact economics remain declared sensitivity assumptions, not causal forecasts.
presentation.decisionSupported: Prioritize retention investigation and evaluate a bounded contact scenario for the supported repeat-subscriber population.
presentation.evaluationMode: February fit and disjoint calibration holdout, followed by one untouched March test window.
presentation.coverAlt: Subscriber retention analysis dashboard showing material movements, cohort comparisons, and governed metric context

story.recruiterSummary: A full-depth retention analysis system over 442.2 million accepted rows that combines governed descriptive analysis, a carefully scoped churn model, an assumption-bound scenario planner, and a complete zero-cost public data release.
story.technicalNarrative: Compressed sources stream into typed Parquet, then DuckDB and dbt reconstruct subscription state and build cutoff-safe snapshots, cohorts, segments, and metric marts. A calibrated nonlinear challenger is compared with a logistic baseline and is shipped only for repeat subscribers. The public interface is static, while the complete transformed data plane is distributed separately as Parquet.
scalabilityRoadmap: Partition controls and one-thread DuckDB execution already process the full 442.2 million-row corpus locally
A hosted query plane can be added only when a real latency or concurrency requirement justifies recurring compute
Actual Fabric and Power BI engine evidence can reopen only under a separately approved budget
Causal uplift modeling requires randomized intervention, delivery, acceptance, and outcome data that the source does not contain
story.executiveSummary: The project turns a large historical subscription corpus into an auditable decision workflow. It identifies material retention changes, evaluates a calibrated risk model without hiding its population failure, and lets an analyst test finite outreach assumptions. It publishes both the interface and every accepted transformed row while keeping recurring project cost and public request-time compute at zero.
story.intendedUser: A subscription lifecycle analyst or retention lead reviewing renewal behavior, engagement change, historical churn risk, and finite contact capacity.

example.title: Investigating a retention movement before planning outreach
steps: Open the overview and identify a material movement rather than reading isolated KPI cards

In private mode, review the supported repeat-subscriber risk population
Run low, base, and high assumed-lift cases with one fixed selected set and explicit spend

technologyDecisions.technology: DuckDB, dbt Core, and partitioned Parquet
technologyDecisions.rationale: They preserve full analytical detail and governed SQL semantics on one machine without a managed warehouse bill.
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Local batch execution has no shared concurrency or provider-native monitoring.

technologyDecisions.rationale: The public analytical product fits in governed extracts and needs no request-time private data access.
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Public subscriber drill-down and arbitrary queries are deliberately unavailable.

technologyDecisions.rationale: It publishes every transformed accepted row with file delivery and dataset browsing at zero recurring project cost.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Object storage plus a custom catalog or live query API
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Users download or query Parquet rather than receiving an interactive hosted warehouse endpoint.

technologyDecisions.technology: Calibrated histogram gradient boosting with a logistic baseline
technologyDecisions.rationale: The nonlinear challenger materially improves held-out log loss while calibration and lift remain measurable against a named simple comparator.
technologyDecisions.alternative: One model reported without a baseline or population gate
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Probability use is restricted to repeat subscribers and cannot cover the high-churn March-new group.

bulletCandidates.bullet: Built a DuckDB and dbt retention warehouse over 442.2 million accepted membership, payment, listening, and churn-label rows, with cutoff and row-reconciliation tests and a complete transformed Parquet release.

Scoped a calibrated churn challenger to 881,701 supported repeat subscribers after the March-new population failed calibration, achieving 5.57 percent lower log loss, 0.0166 ECE, and 4.95 top-decile lift on an untouched test window.
Designed an exception-led retention workflow that separates observed cohort movement, modeled historical churn risk, and user-assumed scenario economics, with zero formula reconciliation error.
Published 442,211,685 transformed rows as 32 Zstandard-compressed Parquet files and deployed the analysis product with zero public request-time compute and zero recurring project cost.
